cause: QuestObjectScope restricted targeting/visibility and descendant lifetime, but the native loot containers did not retain that scope. Direct StoreLootItem, forged creature/GO/Loot GUID packets, cached currency/FFA responses, money and master distribution could bypass the quest owner or consume a cancelled source-less container. The native pre-fix library actually reproduces these receipts; this is not inferred from visibility alone.
implementation: LootMgr keeps mutex-protected weak scopes per container and indices from full source GUID to registered containers and back. WorldObject binding seals both its own loot and already-generated personal containers. Native FillLoot admits the actual scope owner before generation. No strong reference prolongs an accepted quest attempt. Expired/cancelled scopes and different owners fail closed; conflicting uncleared scopes close the container to everyone until native clear.

Native opening, slot/availability/response, direct storage, currency, personal money, autostore packets, master assignment and manual roll-start honor current scope admission. GO/creature source checks also protect release and Fetch/AoE recipient mutation. Native ordinary loot, conditions, group eligibility, inventory errors, full-bag retry and exactly-once storage remain intact. No item, quest, scenario or teleport grant is added.

Native clear removes the weak/source indices and registered Loot GUID before its already-isClear early return, including refused fills and otherwise-empty registered containers. Native Loot/Creature/Player layouts are unchanged: new state is appended only to the global manager. Registered source indexing avoids scanning historical Loot GUID tombstones when a source becomes quest-bound.

Manual roll-start now returns for an absent/invalid source before dereferencing Loot. A private container cannot be forced into another player's roll; native public roll completion/Need/Greed and timeout behavior are retained.
